title: Earth, Oppressed by Demon-Kings, Seeks Brahma
one_line_summary: The Earth, burdened by arrogant demon kings, takes the form of a weeping cow and appeals to Brahma for relief.
source_excerpt: The Earth, crushed by the weight of countless demon kings, assumes the form of a cow, tearful and exhausted, and laments her misery before Brahma. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 16-17)

title: Vishnu Promises to Descend into the House of Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Brahma and the gods carry the Earth's plea to Vishnu on the milk ocean; a divine voice declares Vishnu will be born in Vasudeva's house and that the gods should descend as helpers.
source_excerpt: Brahma, bearing the Earth, goes with the gods to the shore of the milk ocean; a voice from the sky declares that the Supreme Lord himself will be born in Vasudeva's home, and the gods should descend in part to aid him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 18-24)

title: The Divine Voice Warns Kamsa of His Slayer
one_line_summary: At Vasudeva's wedding procession, Kamsa drives the chariot and hears a bodiless voice declare that Devaki's eighth child will slay him.
source_excerpt: As Kamsa drives the chariot bearing the newly-wed Vasudeva and Devaki, a bodiless voice warns him: the eighth child of the woman he escorts will be his death. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 28-33)

title: Vasudeva Pacifies Kamsa and Promises His Sons
one_line_summary: Kamsa seizes Devaki to kill her, but Vasudeva placates him with reasoning and vows to surrender every newborn son to him.
source_excerpt: Kamsa draws his sword on his own sister, but Vasudeva soothes him with words on death and destiny, promising to hand over each son born to Devaki; at this Kamsa relents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 34-54)

title: Kamsa Imprisons Devaki and Kills Her Sons
one_line_summary: After Narada reveals that the gods are incarnating among the Yadavas, Kamsa imprisons Devaki and Vasudeva and kills each child as it is born.
source_excerpt: Told by Narada that the gods have taken birth among the Yadavas, Kamsa has Devaki and Vasudeva chained in prison and kills every son she bears, one by one. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 55-68)

title: Vishnu Commands Yogamaya to Transfer Balarama
one_line_summary: Vishnu directs Yogamaya to draw the unborn Balarama from Devaki's womb into Rohini's, and to be born herself as Nanda's daughter.
source_excerpt: Vishnu instructs Yogamaya to transfer the unborn Balarama from Devaki's womb into that of Rohini in Gokula, and to take birth herself as the daughter of Nanda and Yasoda. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 4-15)

title: Vishnu Enters Vasudeva and Devaki Conceives
one_line_summary: Vishnu enters Vasudeva's mind; Devaki conceives the Lord and glows with brilliance, and Kamsa, though uneasy, refrains from harming her.
source_excerpt: The Lord enters Vasudeva's heart; Devaki, bearing the whole world's support in her womb, shines so brightly that Kamsa sees in her the presence of his own destroyer, yet he stays his hand. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 15-23)

title: The Gods Praise the Lord Within Devaki's Womb
one_line_summary: Brahma, Shiva and the host of gods descend to praise the unborn Lord in Devaki's womb and then depart.
source_excerpt: Brahma and Shiva, with sages and gods, come to Devaki's prison and praise the unborn Lord who will lift the earth's burden; having sung his glories they return to heaven. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 24-42)

title: Krishna Is Born at Midnight
one_line_summary: At a supremely auspicious hour, with nature rejoicing, Krishna is born of Devaki in the prison at midnight.
source_excerpt: At midnight, as the directions turn calm and all beings rejoice, the Lord appears from Devaki as the full moon rises in the east. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-7)

title: Krishna Reveals His Divine Form and Recalls Past Births
one_line_summary: The infant reveals a four-armed form bearing conch and discus; Vasudeva and Devaki praise him, and he recalls his earlier births to them before resuming an ordinary infant form.
source_excerpt: The newborn shows himself four-armed, holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, adored by his parents; he reminds them of their past births and their long austerities, then becomes an ordinary infant again. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 8-45)

title: Vasudeva Carries Krishna Out of the Prison
one_line_summary: Prompted by the Lord, Vasudeva carries the baby out; the prison doors open by themselves, Shesha shelters them from rain, and the Yamuna parts to give passage.
source_excerpt: The guards are struck with sleep and the prison doors open by themselves; as Vasudeva bears the child through the night, the serpent Shesha spreads his hoods against the rain and the Yamuna parts its waters to let them cross. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-49)

title: Vasudeva Exchanges the Babies
one_line_summary: Vasudeva places Krishna in Yasoda's bed in Nanda's Gokula and carries Yasoda's newborn daughter back to Mathura.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva sets his son in Yasoda's bed in Gokula, takes up the girl-child born there, and returns to the prison, where he lays her beside Devaki and resumes his chains. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 50-52)

title: Kamsa Comes to Slay the Newborn Girl
one_line_summary: Awakened by the guards, Kamsa rushes to the prison and snatches the newborn girl from Devaki, who pleads for her life.
source_excerpt: Hearing of the birth, Kamsa hastens to the lying-in room; the grieving Devaki begs him to spare the infant girl, but he tears the child from her hands. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-6)

title: Yogamaya Rises and Warns Kamsa
one_line_summary: When Kamsa dashes the girl against a stone she rises as the eight-armed goddess Yogamaya, warns him that his slayer is already born, and Kamsa, shaken, repents and frees Devaki and Vasudeva.
source_excerpt: The flung infant springs into the sky as the eight-armed goddess Yogamaya and declares, 'Your slayer is already born elsewhere'; humbled, Kamsa releases Devaki and Vasudeva and begs their forgiveness. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 7-27)

title: Kamsa's Ministers Counsel Slaughtering the Righteous
one_line_summary: Kamsa's demon ministers urge him to kill all newborn children and to destroy the brahmanas, cows and all in whom Vishnu dwells.
source_excerpt: The demon ministers persuade Kamsa to slay every infant in city and village, and to root out the brahmanas, cows and austerity in which, they say, the gods have their life. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 28-41)

title: Kamsa Sends Demons to Destroy the Infants
one_line_summary: Kamsa dispatches shape-shifting demons across the land to massacre the sages' and infants' protectors, and returns to his palace.
source_excerpt: Kamsa sends forth demons who can assume any form, bidding them slaughter the holy everywhere, and himself withdraws into his palace. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 42-46)

title: Nanda Celebrates the Birth of His Son
one_line_summary: Nanda performs the birth rites with lavish gifts of cows and gold, and the whole of Gokula rejoices over the newborn child.
source_excerpt: Nanda performs the birth ceremonies with thousands of adorned cows and heaps of gifts; the cowherd men and women, scented and adorned, pour into his home to bless the child. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-17)

title: Nanda Visits Mathura and Meets Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Nanda goes to Mathura to pay his annual tribute, and Vasudeva joyfully embraces him as a brother.
source_excerpt: Nanda travels to Mathura to pay the yearly tax; Vasudeva, learning of his arrival, rises and embraces him as if life had returned to his body. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 18-20)

title: Vasudeva Warns Nanda of Danger in Gokula
one_line_summary: Vasudeva affectionately inquires after his sons and urges Nanda to return quickly to Gokula, for evil omens are gathering there.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva, anxious for the two boys hidden in Nanda's care, tells him not to linger, for great disturbances are rising in Gokula; Nanda and his men hasten back with their carts. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 21-32)

title: Putana the Child-Slayer Enters Gokula
one_line_summary: Kamsa's agent Putana, a demoness who kills infants, disguises herself as a beautiful woman and enters Nanda's village.
source_excerpt: Putana, sent by Kamsa and wandering among villages killing infants, flies into Gokula and by her magic takes the form of a lovely woman. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-5)

title: The Infant Krishna Drains Putana's Life
one_line_summary: Putana offers the baby her poisoned breast, but Krishna sucks out her very life-breath, and she falls dead, revealing her true demon form.
source_excerpt: Taking the baby to her breast, the demoness is seized in her vital parts; Krishna drinks out her life along with her milk, and with a terrible cry she dies and crashes down in her monstrous true form. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-12)

title: The Villagers Burn Putana's Body
one_line_summary: The gopis perform protective rites over the child, and the cowherds cut up and burn Putana's vast corpse, from which rises a fragrant smoke, for she attained a mother's reward.
source_excerpt: The cowherd women bathe the child and chant protective hymns over him; the men hew Putana's enormous body to pieces and burn it, and a fragrance like aloe rises from the fire, for she was granted the goal of a mother. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 13-33)

title: The Baby's Foot Overturns the Cart
one_line_summary: During the birth ceremonies, the unattended infant kicks the great cart, shattering it and scattering its vessels, to the astonishment of all.
source_excerpt: Left beneath a cart while Yasoda attends the rites, the crying infant kicks it with his tender foot; the cart overturns, its wheels and axle broken and its vessels scattered, leaving everyone amazed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 3-16)

title: Trinavarta the Whirlwind Carries Off the Baby
one_line_summary: Kamsa's servant Trinavarta, in the form of a whirlwind, snatches the child away, blinding Gokula with dust as Yasoda searches in vain.
source_excerpt: The demon Trinavarta, as a whirlwind of dust and grit, sweeps up the child so that Yasoda cannot find him, and the whole village is plunged into darkness and confusion. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-24)

title: Trinavarta Is Crushed by the Child's Weight
one_line_summary: Unable to carry the ever-heavier baby through the sky, Trinavarta falls onto a rock and is crushed, while the child is found safe on his chest.
source_excerpt: The demon, finding the child heavier than a mountain, cannot fly on; seized by the throat, he crashes down upon a rock and is shattered, and the cowherds find Krishna lying safe upon his breast. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 25-32)

title: Yasoda Sees the Universe in the Child's Mouth
one_line_summary: As Yasoda nurses the yawning child, she glimpses the whole cosmos within his open mouth and trembles in wonder.
source_excerpt: While Yasoda fondly looks at her child, he yawns and she beholds within his mouth the sky, the earth, the oceans, the sun and moon, and all beings, and she is struck with awe. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 33-37)

title: Garga Secretly Names Rama and Krishna
one_line_summary: The family priest Garga, sent by Vasudeva, secretly performs the naming ceremony, calling the boys Rama and Krishna, and foretells their glories.
source_excerpt: Garga, coming quietly at Vasudeva's bidding, performs the naming rites in secret: the son of Rohini he names Rama and Balabhadra, and Nanda's son he names Krishna, and he declares that they will dispel all evil. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-19)

title: Krishna and Rama's Childhood Pranks
one_line_summary: The two boys crawl and toddle about Gokula, and Krishna steals butter and curds from the gopis' homes with playful tricks.
source_excerpt: The boys crawl through the mud of Gokula to the delight of all; Krishna, the gopis complain, lets loose the calves, steals curd and butter, and smashes pots when he cannot reach them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-30)

title: Krishna Eats Mud and Shows the Cosmos
one_line_summary: Accused of eating dirt, Krishna opens his mouth before Yasoda, who sees the entire universe within it and is overwhelmed.
source_excerpt: When his playmates accuse him of eating mud, Krishna tells his mother to look in his mouth, and there she beholds the whole world with its mountains, oceans and stars; the Lord then veils her mind again in motherly love. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 31-45)

title: Krishna Breaks the Butter Pot
one_line_summary: While Yasoda churns, the hungry child climbs onto her lap; when she leaves, he breaks the churn-pot, steals the butter and feeds it to the monkeys, then flees as she chases him.
source_excerpt: Interrupted in her churning to nurse the child, Yasoda returns to find the pot shattered and Krishna, with the stolen butter, feeding it to a monkey; he darts away and she pursues him with a stick. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-10)

title: Yasoda Binds Krishna to the Mortar
one_line_summary: Yasoda tries to tie the mischievous Krishna with a rope, but every rope falls short by two fingers, until, moved by her effort, he lets himself be bound.
source_excerpt: However much rope Yasoda joins, it is always two fingers too short to bind him; seeing her toil and sweat, Krishna of his own grace submits and is bound to the mortar. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-20)

title: Krishna Notices the Twin Arjuna Trees
one_line_summary: While his mother is busy, Krishna sees the two arjuna trees that were once the guhyaka sons of Kubera, Nalakuvara and Manigriva.
source_excerpt: Left to himself, Krishna catches sight of the twin arjuna trees, who in a former life had been Nalakuvara and Manigriva, the sons of Kubera. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 21-22)

title: Narada Curses Nalakuvara and Manigriva
one_line_summary: Drunk and naked in a river with celestial women, Kubera's sons insult Narada, who curses them to become twin arjuna trees until Krishna's touch frees them.
source_excerpt: Intoxicated with wine, the two sons of Kubera sport naked with women in the Ganga; the sage Narada, to cure their pride, curses them to stand as twin arjuna trees, promising release at the touch of Vasudeva. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-22)

title: Krishna Uproots the Twin Trees
one_line_summary: Dragging the mortar to which he is tied, the crawling Krishna passes between the two trees and uproots them.
source_excerpt: Pulling the mortar after him, Krishna passes between the two arjuna trees and, with a single tug, brings them crashing down. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 23-26)

title: The Two Devotees Are Liberated
one_line_summary: From the fallen trees emerge two radiant beings who bow to Krishna, praise him, and, released from their curse, depart to the north.
source_excerpt: From the fallen trees rise two brilliant figures who bow to Krishna, extol him as the ancient Lord, and, at his word, depart; the cowherds hear the crash and marvel. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-43)

title: The Fruit-Seller Receives a Gift of Jewels
one_line_summary: Krishna takes grain to barter for fruit, but the fruit-seller's basket fills with gems as her fruit spills into his hands.
source_excerpt: Going out to buy fruit with a fistful of grain, Krishna lets it spill, and the fruit-seller finds her basket filled with jewels where her fruit had been. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-10)

title: Upananda Urges the Move to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Citing the many evil omens that have befallen Gokula, the elder Upananda persuades the cowherds to migrate with their herds.
source_excerpt: The elder Upananda declares that omens threaten the children, and that the whole colony, with its cattle and carts, should depart at once for a safer pasture. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-30)

title: The Cowherds Settle in Vrindavan
one_line_summary: The cowherd community journeys with their herds and carts and settles in Vrindavan, forming their camp in a crescent of wagons.
source_excerpt: With cattle before them and horns sounding, the cowherds travel to Vrindavan and pitch their camp there, delighted with the forest, the Govardhana hill and the banks of the Yamuna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 31-35)

title: Krishna and Balarama Become Calf-Herders and Slay Vatsasura
one_line_summary: The boys take up calf-herding, and Krishna seizes the demon Vatsasura, who has taken the form of a calf, and hurls him dead into a kapittha tree.
source_excerpt: As Krishna and Balarama tend the calves, the demon Vatsasura mingles with the herd in the form of a calf; Krishna whirls him by his hind legs and dashes him lifeless against a tree. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 36-44)

title: Krishna Slays the Crane-Demon Bakasura
one_line_summary: The crane-demon Bakasura, Kamsa's ally, swallows Krishna, but Krishna burns and tears him apart and frees himself.
source_excerpt: The great crane-demon Bakasura gulps down Krishna, but the child sears his palate and then tears the demon apart, to the wonder of the cowherd boys. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-52)

title: Aghasura Becomes a Giant Python
one_line_summary: Aghasura, brother of Putana and Bakasura, takes the form of a vast python and lies with open mouth across the path of the boys.
source_excerpt: The demon Aghasura, eager to avenge his kin, stretches his body into a gigantic python and lies across the path with gaping jaws, which the boys mistake for a mountain cave. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-24)

title: Krishna Kills Aghasura and Revives His Friends
one_line_summary: Entering the demon's throat with his friends, Krishna expands and chokes Aghasura to death, then revives the swallowed boys and calves; the demon's soul merges into Krishna as a great light.
source_excerpt: Krishna enters the demon's mouth and grows until he blocks its throat; as the demon's life departs, Krishna raises up his companions and calves and walks out, while a great radiance from the demon's body enters Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 25-35)

title: Brahma Steals the Calves and Boys
one_line_summary: While Krishna searches for the strayed calves, Brahma, wanting to test the Lord, carries off all the calves and cowherd boys and hides them.
source_excerpt: While the boys are at play, the calves wander off, and as Krishna goes to find them, Brahma secretly carries away both calves and boys, hiding them by his power. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-16)

title: Krishna Expands Into All the Calves and Boys
one_line_summary: To console their mothers, Krishna himself becomes every missing calf and boy, and for a year plays their roles in the cowherd homes.
source_excerpt: Krishna expands himself into every vanished calf and boy, and for a full year each mother unknowingly nurses and loves the Lord himself as her own child, with a love deeper than before. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-26)

title: Brahma Is Bewildered and Worships Krishna
one_line_summary: Returning after a moment of his time, Brahma finds everything as before and, seeing all the boys as four-armed forms of Vishnu, falls at Krishna's feet in humility.
source_excerpt: Bewildered by what he sees, Brahma beholds all the cowherd boys and calves as countless Vishnu-forms and, understanding the Lord's majesty, bows and praises Krishna, who then restores his friends. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-63)

title: Brahma Praises Krishna and Departs
one_line_summary: Brahma hymns Krishna's boundless glories, confesses his own arrogance, and returns to his abode after circumambulating the Lord.
source_excerpt: Brahma pours out a long hymn before Krishna, confessing that even he cannot fathom the Lord's power, and, walking three times around him and bowing, departs for his own realm. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-41)

title: The Boys Resume Their Meal Unaware of the Lost Year
one_line_summary: Krishna returns the boys and calves as before, and, though a year had passed, to them it seemed but a moment, and they finish their picnic and go home.
source_excerpt: Krishna brings the boys and calves back to the sandbank as though nothing had happened; to them the whole year seemed no more than half a moment, and they return, carrying the python's dried skin as a trophy. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 41-47)

title: The Boys Long for the Palm Grove's Fruit
one_line_summary: The cowherd boys ask Krishna and Balarama to take them to the talavana, whose sweet fruit is guarded by the donkey-demon Dhenuka.
source_excerpt: The boys tell Krishna and Balarama of the palm grove whose fragrant fruit lies uneaten because the fierce donkey-demon Dhenuka and his kin guard it. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-26)

title: Balarama Slays Dhenuka
one_line_summary: Balarama shakes the palm trees to bring down the fruit, and when Dhenuka charges, he seizes the donkey and dashes it lifeless against a palm.
source_excerpt: Balarama shakes the palms till the fruit falls; the enraged Dhenuka rushes in, and Balarama, catching him by the hind legs, whirls him and hurls him dead against a great palm. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-34)

title: Krishna and Balarama Clear the Grove of Dhenuka's Kin
one_line_summary: As Dhenuka's kin charge to avenge him, Krishna and Balarama slay them all, and men and beasts freely enjoy the grove.
source_excerpt: Dhenuka's kindred rush upon the brothers and are flung lifeless among the palms, until the grove lies strewn with their bodies and the people and cattle freely enjoy its fruit and grass. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 35-40)

title: Krishna Revives the Cowherds from Poisoned Water
one_line_summary: Thirsty cowherds and cattle drink the poisoned waters of the Yamuna and die; Krishna revives them all with a glance of nectar.
source_excerpt: The cowherds and cattle, overcome by the poisoned water of the Yamuna, fall lifeless, but Krishna, the master of all yoga, restores them with a single nectar-showering glance. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-51)

title: Krishna Leaps Into Kaliya's Poisoned Pool
one_line_summary: Seeing the Yamuna polluted by the serpent Kaliya's venom, Krishna climbs a kadamba tree and plunges into the deep poisoned pool to subdue him.
source_excerpt: Determined to cleanse the Yamuna of Kaliya's poison, Krishna climbs a tall kadamba tree, slaps his arms, and dives into the serpent's deep and venomous pool. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 3-5)

title: Kaliya Seizes Krishna and Vraja Despairs
one_line_summary: Kaliya coils around Krishna and holds him motionless in the depths, while the cowherds, cows and all of Gokula rush to the bank in grief.
source_excerpt: The serpent Kaliya winds his coils about Krishna and holds him in the water; seeing their beloved gripped by the snake, the whole of Vraja, with Nanda and the gopis, comes wailing to the bank. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 8-20)

title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya's Heads
one_line_summary: Breaking free of the serpent's coils, Krishna leaps up and dances upon Kaliya's raised heads, trampling each hood that will not bow.
source_excerpt: Slipping from the coils, Krishna springs onto the serpent's hoods and dances there, crushing each head that refuses to bow, while the celestial beings shower flowers and music upon him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 22-30)

title: Kaliya's Wives Plead for His Life
one_line_summary: The serpent's wives, with disheveled hair and folded hands, praise Krishna and beg him to spare their husband's life.
source_excerpt: As Kaliya lies broken, his wives come before Krishna with folded hands and, praising him, plead that the chastisement itself is grace and that their husband's life be spared. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 30-52)

title: Krishna Spares and Banishes Kaliya
one_line_summary: Krishna spares Kaliya, orders him to leave the Yamuna for the ocean, and Kaliya departs with his family, leaving the river's waters sweet again.
source_excerpt: Krishna bids Kaliya depart with his kin to the ocean, declaring that the mark of Krishna's feet will protect him from Garuda; Kaliya worships him and leaves, and the Yamuna becomes pure and sweet once more. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 53-67)

title: Why Kaliya Took Refuge in the Yamuna
one_line_summary: The sage recounts how Kaliya, having withheld Garuda's tribute and been beaten by him, fled to the Yamuna pool, where a curse forbade Garuda to enter.
source_excerpt: It is told how Kaliya, who had scorned the tribute owed to Garuda, was struck by his wing and fled into the Yamuna; there the sage Saubhari's curse kept Garuda from entering. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

title: Krishna Emerges and the Villagers Rejoice
one_line_summary: Krishna comes out of the pool adorned with gems; the cowherds embrace him, and Nanda gives cattle and gold to the brahmanas for his deliverance.
source_excerpt: Krishna emerges from the pool, and the cowherds, as though their breath had returned, embrace him; Nanda bestows cows and gold upon the brahmanas in thanksgiving for his son's escape. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-18)

title: Krishna Swallows the Forest Fire
one_line_summary: As a forest fire surrounds the sleeping settlement at night, the villagers call on Krishna, who drinks up the fierce flames.
source_excerpt: When a blazing forest fire closes in on the sleeping Vraja, the terrified people cry out to Krishna, and the Lord, of boundless power, drinks the whole fire into himself. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-24)

title: Pralamba Joins the Games in Disguise
one_line_summary: The demon Pralamba, intent on seizing the boys, joins their play disguised as a cowherd, and Krishna, knowing him, allows it, planning his death.
source_excerpt: Pralamba, a demon in cowherd's form, enters the boys' games; Krishna, who knows all, welcomes his friendship while resolving his destruction. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 16-18)

title: Balarama Slays Pralamba
one_line_summary: In the riding game, Pralamba carries Balarama far off and reveals his terrible form, but Balarama strikes his head with a mighty fist and fells him dead.
source_excerpt: When the demon Pralamba, carrying Balarama in the game, flees skyward and shows his giant form, Balarama strikes him once on the head with his fist, and the demon falls dead like a mountain. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 19-29)

title: The Cattle Stray Into the Munja Forest and a Wildfire Breaks Out
one_line_summary: While the boys play, the cattle wander into a dense grove of munja grass, and a fierce wildfire springs up around them.
source_excerpt: The cattle, roaming at will, stray into the munja thicket and are lost, and as the boys search, a great wildfire, driven by the wind, surrounds them and the herds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-8)

title: Krishna Swallows the Wildfire and Saves the Herd
one_line_summary: Krishna bids the terrified cowherds close their eyes, drinks up the flames, and, when they open them, they stand safe at Bhandira.
source_excerpt: Telling them not to fear and to shut their eyes, Krishna drinks the raging fire into his mouth, and the cowherds, opening their eyes, find themselves and their herds delivered at Bhandira. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 9-13)

title: Krishna Enjoys the Monsoon Pastures
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter the rain-washed forest with the herd, and the boys share a simple meal of curd-rice with him on a rock.
source_excerpt: In the rains, Krishna and Balarama lead the cattle into the lush forest, where they picnic on curd and rice set out on a stone and rest among the contented cows. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 24-30)

title: The Gopis Praise Krishna's Flute
one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute in the forest, and the gopis, describing its sweetness to one another, are carried away into his pastimes.
source_excerpt: As Krishna's flute-song sounds through the forest, the gopis tell one another how even the deer, the rivers and the gods are enchanted by it, and they are lost in remembrance of him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-19)

title: The Gopis Perform the Katyayani Vow
one_line_summary: Through the first month of winter, the young gopis bathe in the Yamuna and worship the goddess Katyayani, praying that Krishna become their husband.
source_excerpt: Through the first month of winter the gopis keep their vow, bathing before dawn in the Yamuna and worshipping an image of the goddess, with the single prayer that Nanda's son become their husband. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-5)

title: Krishna Steals the Gopis' Clothes
one_line_summary: Krishna carries off the gopis' garments as they bathe, climbs a kadamba tree, and teasingly bids them come and take them back.
source_excerpt: While the gopis bathe, Krishna gathers up their clothes, climbs a kadamba tree, and, laughing, tells them to come and receive their garments one by one. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-11)

title: Krishna Returns the Clothes and Blesses the Gopis
one_line_summary: The shivering gopis come from the water, and Krishna, pleased with their sincerity, returns their clothes and promises their wish will be fulfilled.
source_excerpt: Coming from the water with hands pressed together, the gopis receive back their garments, and Krishna tells them he has understood their vow, and that their longing for him shall bear its fruit in the coming nights. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-27)

title: The Brahmanas Refuse Krishna's Request for Food
one_line_summary: Hungry, Krishna sends the cowherd boys to ask food of brahmanas performing a sacrifice, but they turn the request away, mistaking Krishna for a mere man.
source_excerpt: Sent by Krishna to beg food from the brahmanas performing the Angirasa sacrifice, the boys are refused, for the ritualists, proud of their learning, do not recognize the Lord. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

title: The Brahmanas' Wives Bring Food to Krishna
one_line_summary: Krishna then sends the boys to the brahmanas' wives, who, longing for his sight, hasten to him with every kind of food, disregarding their families.
source_excerpt: The wives of the brahmanas, hearing that Krishna has come, take dishes of fine food and hurry to him like rivers to the sea, heedless of husbands and kinsmen who would stop them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-19)

title: The Wives Refuse to Return and Krishna Welcomes Them
one_line_summary: The brahmana wives, granted Krishna's sight, refuse to return to their homes, and Krishna, pleased with their devotion, assures them of his grace and sends them back with their minds fixed on him.
source_excerpt: Falling at Krishna's feet, the wives declare they have no refuge but him and will not return; Krishna welcomes them and, teaching that he is won by remembrance rather than by nearness, sends them home with hearts fixed on him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-31)

title: The Brahmanas Repent and Praise Krishna
one_line_summary: Reflecting that their wives' devotion surpassed their own empty rituals, the brahmanas lament their blindness and sing Krishna's praise, longing to see him.
source_excerpt: Realizing that the Lord they had spurned was Vishnu himself, the brahmanas reproach their own pride and empty rites, and, praising Krishna, yearn for his sight yet do not dare approach, fearing Kamsa. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 32-51)
